-- One row per day: the latest landed version of each date.
-- The raw table keeps every version (yearly files plus daily incremental files that refetch
-- the last two weeks, because recent days get revised); latest _ingested_at wins.

WITH source AS (

    SELECT * FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311"."raw_weather_daily"

),

ranked AS (

    SELECT
        *,
        row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY local_date ORDER BY _ingested_at DESC) AS version_rank
    FROM source

)

SELECT
    local_date,
    mean_temperature,
    min_temperature,
    max_temperature,
    total_precipitation,
    total_rain,
    total_snow,
    snow_on_ground,
    -- ECCC reports the gust direction in tens of degrees (0 to 36), so multiply by 10
    direction_max_gust * 10 AS max_gust_direction_deg,
    speed_max_gust,
    cooling_degree_days,
    heating_degree_days,
    min_rel_humidity,

    -- false for days where the station reported nothing at all (all-null rows)
    COALESCE(
        mean_temperature, min_temperature, max_temperature, total_precipitation, total_rain,
        total_snow, snow_on_ground, direction_max_gust, speed_max_gust, cooling_degree_days,
        heating_degree_days, min_rel_humidity
    ) IS NOT NULL AS has_observations,

    _ingested_at
FROM ranked
WHERE version_rank = 1

-- One row per calendar day, from 2010 (the earliest requests) to a year ahead.
WITH DAYS AS (

    -- cast: Athena can return the sequence as timestamps, which CTAS cannot store here
    SELECT CAST(d AS DATE) AS date_day
    FROM UNNEST(SEQUENCE(DATE '2010-01-01', DATE_ADD('day', 365, CURRENT_DATE), INTERVAL '1' DAY)) AS t(d)

)

SELECT
    (year(date_day) * 10000 + month(date_day) * 100 + day(date_day))                                   AS date_key,
    date_day,
    YEAR(date_day)                                               AS year_num,
    QUARTER(date_day)                                            As quarter_num,
    MONTH(date_day)                                              AS month_num,
    FORMAT_DATETIME(CAST(date_day AS timestamp), 'MMMM')         AS month_name,
    FORMAT_DATETIME(CAST(date_day AS timestamp), 'yyyy-MM')      AS year_month,
    DAY(date_day)                                                AS day_of_month,
    DAY_OF_WEEK(date_day)                                        AS day_of_week_num,   -- 1 = Monday
    FORMAT_DATETIME(CAST(date_day AS timestamp), 'EEEE')         AS day_name,
    DAY_OF_WEEK(date_day) IN (6, 7)                              AS is_weekend
FROM DAYS

WITH source AS (

    SELECT * FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311"."raw_service_requests"

),

-- S4.0 The raw table keeps every stored version of a request (monthly files plus the daily
-- incremental files). The newest updated_date wins; _ingested_at breaks ties and decides
-- when updated_date is null.
ranked AS (

    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY service_request_id
            ORDER BY updated_date DESC NULLS LAST, _ingested_at DESC
        ) AS version_rank
    FROM source

),

latest AS (

    SELECT * FROM ranked
    WHERE version_rank = 1
      AND status_description <> 'TO BE DELETED'

),

-- S5.1 Trim text, collapse repeated spaces, and turn N/A, null, None and blanks into null.
trimmed AS (

    SELECT
        service_request_id,
        -- 5.4 dates are day grain: only recent years are all midnight, so a date is the one
        -- grain that is consistent across years
        CAST(requested_date AS DATE) AS requested_date,
        CAST(updated_date AS DATE)   AS updated_date,
        CAST(closed_date AS DATE)    AS closed_date,
        status_description,
        source,
        case
        when upper(trim(regexp_replace(service_name, '\s+', ' '))) in ('N/A', 'NULL', 'NONE', '') then null
        else trim(regexp_replace(service_name, '\s+', ' '))
    end       AS raw_service_name,
        case
        when upper(trim(regexp_replace(agency_responsible, '\s+', ' '))) in ('N/A', 'NULL', 'NONE', '') then null
        else trim(regexp_replace(agency_responsible, '\s+', ' '))
    end AS agency_responsible,
        case
        when upper(trim(regexp_replace(comm_code, '\s+', ' '))) in ('N/A', 'NULL', 'NONE', '') then null
        else trim(regexp_replace(comm_code, '\s+', ' '))
    end          AS comm_code,
        case
        when upper(trim(regexp_replace(comm_name, '\s+', ' '))) in ('N/A', 'NULL', 'NONE', '') then null
        else trim(regexp_replace(comm_name, '\s+', ' '))
    end          AS comm_name,
        case
        when upper(trim(regexp_replace(location_type, '\s+', ' '))) in ('N/A', 'NULL', 'NONE', '') then null
        else trim(regexp_replace(location_type, '\s+', ' '))
    end      AS location_type,
        longitude,
        latitude,
        _ingested_at                           AS ingested_at
    FROM latest

),

-- S5.2 Retired services carry a leading z / Z / ZZZ / Z CT marker, or one of the words below.
-- Flag from the original name, then strip the marker.
named AS (

    SELECT
        *,
        COALESCE(
            regexp_like(raw_service_name, '^[Zz]+(\s*-\s*|\s+)')
            OR regexp_like(raw_service_name, '^ZParks\b')
            OR regexp_like(raw_service_name, '\bOLD\b|DO NOT USE|INTERNAL'),
            false
        ) AS is_legacy_service,
        regexp_replace(
            regexp_replace(raw_service_name, '^ZParks\b', 'Parks'),
            '^[Zz]+(?:\s*-\s*|\s+)', ''
        ) AS name_no_marker
    FROM trimmed

)

-- S5.3 Known prefix variants. Every remaining spelling variant is mapped to its most common
-- spelling in service_name_map.
SELECT
    service_request_id,
    requested_date,
    updated_date,
    closed_date,
    status_description,
    source,
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            REGEXP_REPLACE(name_no_marker, '^Mayors Office\b', 'Mayor''s Office'),
            '^City Clerks\b', 'City Clerk''s'
        ),
        '^REDS\b', 'RE&DS'
    ) AS service_name_fixed,
    is_legacy_service,
    agency_responsible,
    comm_code,
    comm_name,
    location_type,
    longitude,
    latitude,
    ingested_at
FROM named

-- Maps each spelling variant of a service name to its most common spelling. Variants are names
-- that match once case and punctuation are ignored, for example "Roads - Streetlight Damage" and
-- "Roads - Streetlight - Damage". Only variants that differ from their canonical name are listed.
-- It is computed from the data on every run, so new variants are picked up automatically.
-- Ties go to the alphabetically first spelling, so the result is stable.

WITH spellings AS (

    SELECT
        service_name_fixed                                          AS variant_name,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(service_name_fixed), '[^a-z0-9]', '')  AS match_key,
        COUNT(*)                                                    AS requests
    FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_intermediate"."base_service_requests"
    WHERE service_name_fixed IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 1, 2

),

ranked AS (

    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY match_key
            ORDER BY requests DESC, variant_name
        ) AS spelling_rank
    FROM spellings
    WHERE match_key <> ''

),

canonical AS (

    SELECT match_key, variant_name AS canonical_name
    FROM ranked
    WHERE spelling_rank = 1

)

SELECT
    s.variant_name,
    c.canonical_name
FROM ranked s
JOIN canonical c ON c.match_key = s.match_key
WHERE s.variant_name <> c.canonical_name

from "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."service_name_map"

select canonical_name
from "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."service_name_map"
where canonical_name is null

-- One row per service request: the latest landed version, typed and cleaned.
-- base_service_requests does the dedupe and the first cleaning pass; this model maps service
-- names to their canonical spelling and adds the derived columns. The rules come from the
-- exploration notebook (data_exploration.ipynb); the section numbers refer to it.

WITH mapped AS (

    SELECT
        b.*,
        COALESCE(m.canonical_name, b.service_name_fixed) AS service_name
    FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_intermediate"."base_service_requests" b
    LEFT JOIN "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."service_name_map" m
        ON m.variant_name = b.service_name_fixed

),

-- S5.4 Service group, communities and channel.
cleaned AS (

    SELECT
        service_request_id,
        requested_date,
        updated_date,
        closed_date,

        status_description,
        source                       AS channel,
        CASE WHEN source = 'App' THEN 'App' ELSE 'Other channels' END AS channel_group,
        -- before March 2021 the Phone, Web and Other split is reliable; afterwards Web and then
        -- Phone are recorded as Other (notebook section 10)
        requested_date < DATE '2021-03-01' AS is_channel_detail_reliable,

        service_name,
        split_part(service_name, ' - ', 1) AS service_group,
        is_legacy_service,
        agency_responsible,

        comm_code,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(comm_name, '\s*/\s*', '/') AS comm_name,
        COALESCE(
            REGEXP_LIKE(REGEXP_REPLACE(comm_name, '\s*/\s*', '/'), '^\d{2}[A-Z]$'),
            false
        ) AS is_unnamed_area,
        location_type,

        longitude,
        latitude,

        status_description IN ('Closed', 'Duplicate (Closed)')           AS is_closed,
        status_description IN ('Duplicate (Closed)', 'Duplicate (Open)') AS is_duplicate,

        ingested_at,

        CASE
            WHEN closed_date IS NOT NULL THEN date_diff('day', requested_date, closed_date)
        END AS days_open

    FROM mapped

),

-- S7. Backlog cleanups: a closed date and service group with many closures of long-open requests.
BATCHES AS (

    SELECT closed_date, service_group
    FROM cleaned
    WHERE closed_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY closed_date, service_group
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000
       AND approx_percentile(days_open, 0.5) >= 100

)

SELECT
    c.service_request_id,
    c.requested_date,
    c.updated_date,
    c.closed_date,

    c.status_description,
    c.channel,
    c.channel_group,
    c.is_channel_detail_reliable,

    c.service_name,
    c.service_group,
    c.is_legacy_service,
    c.agency_responsible,

    c.comm_code,
    c.comm_name,
    c.is_unnamed_area,
    c.location_type,
    c.longitude,
    c.latitude,

    c.is_closed,
    c.is_duplicate,

    -- status is the source of truth; flag rows where the closed date disagrees with it
    (c.is_closed AND c.closed_date IS NULL)
      OR ((NOT c.is_closed) AND c.closed_date IS NOT NULL)              AS has_status_date_conflict,

    CASE
        WHEN c.is_closed AND c.closed_date IS NOT NULL AND c.closed_date >= c.requested_date
            THEN c.days_open
    END                                                                  AS days_to_close,

    -- part of a backlog cleanup, and itself open for at least the threshold
    COALESCE(
        b.closed_date IS NOT NULL AND c.days_open >= 100,
        false
    )                                                                    AS is_bulk_closure,

    c.ingested_at

FROM cleaned c
LEFT JOIN BATCHES b
    ON b.closed_date = c.closed_date
   AND b.service_group = c.service_group

-- One row per responsible agency. The prefix is the department code (for example CS, TRAN, UEP).
-- Agencies are renamed over time, so the same service can appear under more than one agency.
SELECT
    to_hex(md5(to_utf8(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(agency_responsible as varchar), '')))))          AS agency_key,
    COALESCE(agency_responsible, 'Unknown')               AS agency_name,
    COALESCE(split_part(agency_responsible, ' - ', 1), 'Unknown') AS agency_prefix
FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."stg_service_requests"
GROUP BY agency_responsible

-- One row per cleaned service name. The responsible agency has its own dimension (dim_agency),
-- because services change agencies when the city reorganizes. The legacy flag stays on the fact
-- table: one cleaned name can be reached through both a retired and a current spelling.
SELECT
    to_hex(md5(to_utf8(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(service_name as varchar), ''))))) AS service_key,
    COALESCE(service_name, 'Unknown')     AS service_name,
    COALESCE(service_group, 'Unknown')    AS service_group
FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."stg_service_requests"
GROUP BY service_name, service_group

-- One row per community code. Requests with no community share the "UNKNOWN" row.
-- The source gives community centrepoints, not addresses, and the points within one community
-- differ by a few metres, so each community gets the median point. Numeric area codes such as
-- 01H are areas, not places, so they have no coordinates.
SELECT
    to_hex(md5(to_utf8(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(comm_code as varchar), '')))))           AS community_key,
    COALESCE(comm_code, 'UNKNOWN')               AS community_code,
    COALESCE(MAX(comm_name), 'Unknown')          AS community_name,
    COALESCE(bool_or(is_unnamed_area), false)    AS is_unnamed_area,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(bool_or(is_unnamed_area), false) THEN NULL
         ELSE approx_percentile(longitude, 0.5) END AS centre_longitude,
    case when COALESCE(bool_or(is_unnamed_area), false) THEN NULL
         ELSE approx_percentile(latitude, 0.5) END AS centre_latitude
FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."stg_service_requests"
GROUP BY comm_code

-- One row per channel. Use channel_group (App or Other channels) for trends across all years;
-- the full channel split is only reliable before March 2021 (see is_channel_detail_reliable).
SELECT DISTINCT
    to_hex(md5(to_utf8(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(channel as varchar), ''))))) AS channel_key,
    COALESCE(channel, 'Unknown')     AS channel,
    channel_group
FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."stg_service_requests"

-- For time to close, use days_to_close and exclude is_bulk_closure; prefer the median.

    to_hex(md5(to_utf8(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(comm_code as varchar), '')))))                            AS community_key,

    is_legacy_service,

-- One row per day from 2012-01-01 to today: 311 volumes joined to that day's weather.
-- Data is complete from 2012-01-01. Days before the weather starts (2012-07-12) and days with
-- no mean temperature have has_temperature = false and null weather values; days with no
-- observations at all have has_weather = false.
-- median_days_to_close covers only requests that have closed and leaves out bulk closures,
-- so recent days read low.

WITH daily AS (

    SELECT
        requested_date_key AS date_key,
        count_if(NOT is_duplicate) AS requests,
        count_if(is_duplicate) AS duplicate_requests,
        count_if(is_closed AND NOT is_duplicate) AS requests_closed,
        approx_percentile(
            CASE WHEN NOT is_duplicate AND NOT is_bulk_closure THEN days_to_close END, 0.5
        ) AS median_days_to_close
    FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_marts"."fct_service_requests"
    GROUP BY 1

)

SELECT
    d.date_key,
    d.date_day,

    COALESCE(daily.requests, 0)           AS requests,
    COALESCE(daily.duplicate_requests, 0) AS duplicate_requests,
    COALESCE(daily.requests_closed, 0)    AS requests_closed,
    daily.median_days_to_close,

    COALESCE(w.has_observations, false)   AS has_weather,
    w.mean_temperature IS NOT NULL        AS has_temperature,
    w.mean_temperature,
    w.min_temperature,
    w.max_temperature,
    w.total_precipitation,
    w.total_rain,
    w.total_snow,
    w.snow_on_ground,
    w.speed_max_gust,
    w.min_rel_humidity
FROM "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_marts"."dim_date" d
LEFT JOIN daily ON daily.date_key = d.date_key
LEFT JOIN "awsdatacatalog"."calgary_311_dbt_staging"."stg_weather_daily" w ON w.local_date = d.date_day
WHERE d.date_day BETWEEN DATE '2012-01-01' AND current_date
